theme: The watchman renewed; the shepherds; the mountains of Israel
readingInstruction: Read Ezekiel 33:1-35:15. The news that Jerusalem has fallen reaches Babylon, and Ezekiel’s tone changes. God renews the watchman’s call and then turns on the false shepherds of Israel and promises to be the shepherd himself. Read chapter 34 slowly.
settingTheScene: In 585 BC, a fugitive from Jerusalem arrived in Babylon with the news that the city had fallen. Ezekiel’s long silence ended, and he began to speak with a new message: hope. The first part of his book was about judgment. The next is about restoration. Chapter 33 reconfirms his role as a watchman and renews God’s appeal to repent. Chapter 34 is one of the greatest chapters on shepherds in the Bible.
observation: “So you, son of man, I have made a watchman for the house of Israel” (33:7).
“As I live, declares the Lord GOD, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from his way and live” (33:11).
“Behold, you are to them like one who sings lustful songs with a beautiful voice and plays well on an instrument, for they hear what you say, but they will not do it” (33:32).
“Woe to the shepherds of Israel who have been feeding themselves! Should not shepherds feed the sheep?” (34:2).
“The weak you have not strengthened, the sick you have not healed, the injured you have not bound up” (34:4).
“Behold, I, I myself will search for my sheep and will seek them out” (34:11).
“I will make them lie down, declares the Lord GOD. I will seek the lost, and I will bring back the strayed” (34:15-16).
“And I will set up over them one shepherd, my servant David, and he shall feed them” (34:23).
interpretation:
The news of Jerusalem’s fall releases Ezekiel from his silence. God renews his commission as watchman. The principle is repeated: if the watchman sees danger and warns, he has done his duty. If not, the blood is on his hands. And God restates the call to repentance of chapter 18: “Turn back, turn back from your evil ways, for why will you die, O house of Israel?” The people still say, “Our transgressions are upon us… how then can we live?” God’s answer is always the same: turn and live.

Verse 32 is a sober observation. The people come to hear Ezekiel as if he were an entertainer. They enjoy the sermon like a beautiful song, but do not act on it. Hearing without doing is the persistent danger.

Chapter 34 is the heart of this section. God condemns the shepherds, meaning the leaders, who have fed themselves and not the flock. They have not strengthened the weak or healed the sick or sought the lost. They have ruled with force and harshness. As a result, the sheep were scattered. God declares that he is against the shepherds. Then comes the most comforting passage: “I, I myself will search for my sheep and will seek them out.” Again and again God says what he will do: search, rescue, gather, bring, feed, make them lie down, seek the lost, bind up the injured, strengthen the weak. He will be the shepherd himself.

And then the promise: “I will set up over them one shepherd, my servant David.” God will shepherd through a king of David’s line, and make a covenant of peace, so that the wild beasts cease from the land, showers of blessing come, and the sheep live securely.

The people of God are described as “my sheep, human sheep, and I am your God.” It is among the most intimate pictures of the relationship between God and his people.
connection: Jesus says, “I am the good shepherd” (John 10:11), and lives out chapter 34: he seeks the lost (Luke 19:10), heals the sick, and binds up the brokenhearted. Luke 15:4-7 tells the story of the shepherd who seeks the one lost sheep. Matthew 9:36 shows him having compassion on the crowds because they were “like sheep without a shepherd.” 1 Peter 5:1-4 calls elders to shepherd the flock willingly, as examples, and promises the unfading crown from the chief Shepherd. Hebrews 13:20 calls him the great shepherd.
application:
Thank Jesus for being the shepherd who searched for you.

If you have a role of leadership, ask whether you are feeding the flock or feeding yourself. Pray for pastors and church leaders.

Look for a “strayed” or “injured” sheep near you, and reach out to them.
prayerPrompts: Thank the Good Shepherd for seeking the lost and binding up the injured.
Ask him to strengthen you where you are weak.
Pray for the shepherds you know.
